shortDescription: Shares of JetBlue NASDAQ:JBLU fell to a record low on Thursday with short interest climbing to more than 30% of float as Wall Street braces for the carrier’s third quarter results on October 27. Like most major U.S. carriers, JetBlue
no longer uses forward contracts to lock in jet fuel prices. This leaves JetBlue

vulnerable to the volatility in the market, namely in an environment of rising prices. Since October 2025, jet fuel prices have risen 120%, translating into an additional cost of approximately $2.5B for JetBlue
This will likely be reflected in JetBlue’s
bottom line in the third quarter, in which the carrier is expected to report an adjusted loss of $0.55 per share, 41% wider than a year ago, even as revenue is expected to increase by 22% to $2.83B.

warned that cost per available seat mile excluding fuel (CASM-ex) would increase by 6% to 8%, an increase from an earlier estimate of CASM-ex of 2.5% to 4.5%, and also lowered its available seat miles (ASM) estimate to a range of 1.5% and 3.5% from 3% to 6%, previously.
These adjustments were based on disruptions due to bad weather and air traffic control issues during the summer that limited the number of seats available to sell to passengers.
Mitigating some of this impact are higher fares. JetBlue
forecasts revenue per available seat mile (RASM) to increase by 17% to 20% from a prior estimate of up 12.5% to 16.5%.
Unfortunately, Wall Street is all too aware this is unlikely to fully offset the surging cost for jet fuel.

title: JetBlue hits record low as Wall Street braces for fuel-driven pressure on Q3 results
